▸ Are LLMs still surprisingly bad at some simple tasks?

💡 A follow-up benchmark shows LLMs still fail simple deterministic tasks by hallucinating answers, requiring constant manual verification.

A one-year follow-up benchmark evaluating leading LLMs on a deterministic set-intersection task—matching top-level domains (TLDs) to valid HTML5 elements—showed that most models still fail despite recent technical advancements. Models exhibited superficial reasoning by hallucinating tags, missing standard elements like `<data>`, padding outputs with irrelevant "near misses," and ignoring technical edge cases such as Punycode TLDs and embedded MathML. In contrast, Siri successfully provided the correct answer only by bypassing generative modeling to directly retrieve data from an existing web page via traditional search. Ultimately, the test demonstrates that LLMs frequently produce confident, plausible-sounding filler for simple factual lookups, reinforcing that they require constant manual verification unlike deterministic tools.

📝 关键要点 (6 sections)
  • Retesting LLM Performance: The author re-evaluated leading AI models one year after an initial benchmark to test if they improved on a straightforward set-intersection question. Despite technical advancements, most models still failed to provide accurate results.
  • The Benchmark Query: The experiment asked models to identify top-level domains (TLDs) that share exact names with valid HTML5 elements. This deterministic task requires comparing two finite, publicly available lists without factual errors.
  • Hallucinations and Inaccuracies: Models like Gemini Flash hallucinated non-existent TLDs and HTML tags, while reasoning models missed standard tags like `<data>` and `search`. Other models padded responses with irrelevant 'near misses' to appear thorough.
  • Siri's Surprising Win: Siri successfully provided the correct answer, but only because it directly retrieved data from an existing web page. This highlights how traditional web search can beat generative LLMs on factual lookup tasks.
  • Unhandled Technical Nuances: Models completely overlooked edge cases like Punycode TLDs matching valid HTML custom elements and allowed embedded MathML tags. These technical omissions demonstrate the superficial nature of LLM reasoning.
  • Risks of AI Sycophancy: LLMs often generate confident, plausible-sounding filler that misleads uncritical users into accepting incorrect data. Unlike deterministic tools like spreadsheets, LLMs require constant manual verification.
